description: This course covers foundational and advanced topics in network security and defense, including cryptographic algorithms such as AES, RSA, and Diffie-Hellman key exchange; network protocols like TCP/IP, HTTP, and DNS; and security mechanisms like firewalls, intrusion detection systems (IDS), and virtual private networks (VPN). Students will explore secure socket layer (SSL)/transport layer security (TLS) protocols, secure hash algorithms (SHA-256), and public key infrastructure (PKI). The course also delves into network defense strategies, including penetration testing, vulnerability assessment, and incident response planning. Topics extend to network segmentation, secure routing protocols (OSPF, BGP), and security policies. Students will analyze attack vectors such as DDoS, man-in-the-middle (MITM), and SQL injection, and evaluate tools like Wireshark, Nmap, and Metasploit for network security analysis and defense.

clos.text: Define cryptographic algorithms such as AES, RSA, and Diffie-Hellman and explain their role in securing data transmission.
Describe network protocols like TCP/IP, HTTP, and DNS and their vulnerabilities to cyber attacks.
Explain secure socket layer (SSL)/transport layer security (TLS) protocols and their implementation in web communications.
Apply network defense techniques such as firewall configuration and intrusion detection system (IDS) deployment to secure enterprise networks.
Design and implement a secure network architecture using tools like Wireshark, Nmap, and Metasploit to analyze and defend against cyber threats.

topics: Introduction to Network Security and Defense
SQL Injection and Web Application Security
